title: Overview of formaldehyde regulations and compliance testing in the EU
date_evidence: On-page byline under the article title: 'published January 13, 2026'
key_claim: The forcing function, testing-laboratory framing: an accredited materials-testing laboratory confirms that from 6 August 2026 REACH Annex XVII entry 77 (Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/1464) caps formaldehyde release from furniture and wood-based articles at 0.062 mg/m3 - exactly half the current E1 threshold of 0.124 mg/m3 - measured by the EN 717-1 chamber method, so many manufacturers must adjust production processes or reformulate binder resins to keep wood-based boards and panels on the EU market.
verbatim_quote: As the new REACH limit of 0.062 mg/m3 is half the current E1 threshold, many manufacturers will have to adjust their production processes to ensure wood-based boards and panels comply with the new restriction by August 2026.
verbatim_list: 0.062 mg/m3 for furniture and wood-based articles
notes: Tier 2: an ISO-accredited, Bureau Veritas-certified independent materials-testing laboratory (Helsinki) writing in a technical-explainer capacity, authored by a named MSc construction-materials-and-fire-testing specialist and footnoted to the primary regulation and the ECHA measurement guideline. This is the better-tier formaldehyde-cliff anchor that replaces the previously held Tier 3 Notifix trade-press item: it states the 6 August 2026 date, the 0.062 mg/m3 / E05 limit, the halving of the E1 threshold and the EN 717-1 test basis from a notified-testing-institute perspective, and it makes clear the binder resin is the primary emission source and the reason reformulation is required. Fills role 1 (the forcing function / formaldehyde cliff).

publisher: Fraunhofer Institute for Wood Research, Wilhelm-Klauditz-Institut WKI
title: Turning residual materials into resources: Bio-based adhesives for wood-based materials (Press release 2025/11)
date_evidence: On-page dateline directly under headline: 'Press release / October 02, 2025'; also 'Last modified: October 02, 2025'
key_claim: The bio-based consensus, from the leading wood-research institute: Fraunhofer WKI's 'LowEPanel' project is developing and scaling formaldehyde-free particleboard adhesives based on lignin and hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF), positioning bio-based binders - not inorganic chemistry - as the 'key technology' and 'promising growth market' for sustainable formaldehyde-free wood bonding, with the entire value chain from raw-material suppliers to particle-board manufacturers covered.
verbatim_quote: In our new “LowEPanel” project, we are working with our partners on the further development and optimization of lignin-HMF resins for the production of particle boards. The entire value chain is covered within the project: from raw-material suppliers, through material and process development, large-scale resin synthesis and dosing technology, and on to particle-board manufacturers.
notes: Tier 2: official press release from a Fraunhofer institute, Europe's leading wood-research institution, the institutional voice of the wood-based-materials sector. STRUCTURAL ANCHOR (flagged): dated 2 October 2025, which falls just before the 24 November 2025 in-window boundary but well within the soft September-2025 allowance, and it is the single most authoritative and canonical statement of the bio-based consensus the scan argues against. Fills role 3 (the bio-based consensus): it shows that institutional R&D money, narrative and effort are flowing into lignin/HMF bio-binders, framing them as THE formaldehyde-free route - the exact green narrative beneath which the scan locates the quiet pMDI swap and the overlooked silicate option. Note the project itself is still at scale-up stage (large-scale resin synthesis and dosing technology are open work items), implicit evidence that bio-based is not yet the at-scale 2026 compliance answer.

title: Development of a Mineral Binder for Wood Wool Acoustic Panels with a Reduced Carbon Footprint
date_evidence: meta-prism.publicationDate: 2025-11-01 / meta-dc.date: 2025-11-01 / on-page: 'Submission received: 19 September 2025 / Revised: 22 October 2025 / Accepted: 27 October 2025 / Published: 1 November 2025'
key_claim: The silicate signal's wood-panel evidence leg: peer-reviewed research on inorganic mineral binders for wood (wood wool) panels shows that incorporating aluminosilicate additives - metakaolin plus liquid glass (sodium silicate solution) - with high-speed disintegration significantly raises mechanical performance (flexural strengths up to 2.65 MPa) and that liquid glass improves durability, water resistance and interfacial bonding between wood particles and binder, validating aluminosilicate/silicate chemistry as a workable formaldehyde-free, non-fossil binder family for wood-based panels.
verbatim_quote: Incorporating aluminosilicate additives, particularly MK and liquid glass, combined with a high-speed disintegration process (5000 rpm), significantly enhances the mechanical properties of wood particleboard composites. Samples containing 20–30% metakaolin and liquid glass achieved peak flexural strengths up to 2.65 MPa and densities exceeding 490 kg/m3, representing substantial improvements over control samples without additives.
notes: Tier 2: peer-reviewed primary research (DOI 10.3390/ma18214999), Materials 2025, 18(21), 4999, from a research-institute team; classified Tier 2 rather than Tier 1 because it functions in this base as the institutional silicate/aluminosilicate WOOD-panel evidence leg (a research-institute source on inorganic binders for wood panels) rather than as canonical primary literature. STRUCTURAL ANCHOR (flagged): published 1 November 2025, just before the 24 November in-window boundary but inside the soft September-2025 allowance; it is the freshest peer-reviewed source putting silicate/aluminosilicate binders onto an actual wood-panel substrate, giving the silicate signal a proper wood-based-panel leg beyond the single kraft-paper-composite study. Fills role 4 (the weak signal) on a wood substrate AND doubles as genuine sourced counter-evidence: the paper's own life-cycle assessment finds the aluminosilicate systems generate 7.11-7.92 kg CO2 eq./m2 versus a 5.40 kg CO2 eq./m2 cement-chip baseline - a real environmental trade-off - and the systems still rely on Portland or calcium-aluminate cement, evidencing that inorganic binder routes carry their own scale-up, CO2 and durability caveats.

title: Screening high-quality lignins extracted from biomass to prepare biobased wood adhesives
key_claim: The bio-based consensus: institutional R&D and the sustainability narrative for formaldehyde-free wood bonding are dominated by bio-based routes, here a peer-reviewed protocol for lignin-based wood adhesives, which itself concedes that 'large-scale production and adoption of lignin-phenol-formaldehyde resin adhesives remain limited owing to challenges related to appearance, performance and cost.'
verbatim_quote: However, the large-scale production and adoption of lignin-phenol-formaldehyde resin adhesives remain limited owing to challenges related to appearance, performance and cost.
notes: Tier 1: peer-reviewed primary research / methods protocol in a Nature journal. STRUCTURAL ANCHOR (the single 3-6m source): it is the freshest canonical primary source establishing that the institutional formaldehyde-free agenda is bio-based (lignin / 5-HMF), the framing the scan pushes against. The scan's freshest bio-based primary literature genuinely sits just before the 3-month window; this is the cleanest in-band example. Fills role 3 (bio-based consensus). Note its candid admission of bio-based scale-up limits.

title: Improved Performance in Multilayer Paper Composites Through the Incorporation of Inorganic Nanomaterials into Sodium Silicate Adhesive
date_evidence: meta-dc.date: 2026-05-05  /  on-page: 'Submission received: 26 February 2026 / Revised: 3 April 2026 / Accepted: 2 May 2026 / Published: 5 May 2026'
key_claim: The weak signal: 2026 peer-reviewed primary research showing that the historic performance gap of inorganic sodium silicate (water glass) adhesive can be closed with modified / hybrid formulations - here incorporating 0.5 wt% nanoclay, nanosilica or kaolin raised composite toughness by 25% - validating modified silicate chemistry as a formaldehyde-free, non-fossil binder route.
verbatim_quote: These materials are produced by pressing paper layers bonded with a sodium silicate adhesive; however, their structural performance is often limited by the adhesive's low mechanical strength... the inclusion of 0.5% NA promoted a 25% increase in toughness.
notes: Tier 1: peer-reviewed primary research, DOI 10.3390/ma19091897. Fills role 4 (the weak signal: modified / hybrid silicate adhesive closing the performance gap). Caveat for the scan: the substrate is multilayer kraft-paper composite, not wood-based panels, and the paper explicitly names sodium silicate's 'low mechanical strength' as the problem nanomaterials must overcome - so it doubles as honest counter-evidence on baseline silicate brittleness. It is the only genuine in-window 2026 primary source on inorganic silicate adhesive performance; the dedicated geopolymer / silicate WOOD-adhesive literature all predates the 6-month window.

title: MEDITE SMARTPLY prepares MDF panels for new EU REACH formaldehyde emission restriction
key_claim: The pMDI reality, producer-confirmed: a leading EU engineered-wood-panel manufacturer (MEDITE SMARTPLY) is transitioning its full MDF range to E05 by 13 April 2026, and states that its products already made with 'no added formaldehyde MDI resins' (MEDITE TRICOYA EXTREME, EXTERIOR, CLEAR, VENT) already meet the stricter limit and need no transition.
verbatim_quote: Products manufactured using no added formaldehyde MDI resins - including MEDITE TRICOYA EXTREME, MEDITE EXTERIOR, MEDITE CLEAR and MEDITE VENT - already meet the stricter emission limit and are not subject to additional transition requirements.
notes: Tier 3: UK construction industry trade publication. Fills role 2 (the pMDI reality) from a producer / industry angle, corroborating the vendor source: the panels that already comply with E05 are the ones bonded with fossil-based MDI resin, evidencing that the quiet compliance swap is to isocyanate chemistry rather than bio-based glue.

title: Geopolymer Market - Industry Analysis, Size, Share, Growth, Trends, and Forecast 2026-2035
date_evidence: On-page: 'Published Date May 2026' (with 'Base Year 2025', 'Forecast Period 2026-2035'); footer 'Copyright (c) 2026'
key_claim: Counter-evidence and market context: geopolymer (alkali-activated aluminosilicate) binders are a fast-growing inorganic-binder class prized for fire resistance and low CO2, but the report's restraints make the bear case - technical performance variability across feedstocks, capital-intensive production, and entrenched preference for incumbent binders - and it treats wood adhesives only as a marginal application versus construction concrete.
verbatim_quote: Technical performance variability across different fly ash compositions and alkaline activator formulations, requiring extensive quality control and material characterization protocols that increase production complexity.
notes: Tier 3: syndicated market-research report (specialist analytical publisher); treat_directionally true because market-research vendors have a selling incentive and the day-precise date is inferred from 'Published Date May 2026'. Fills role 5 (counter-evidence) and the optional market / industry-context role: it documents the structural weaknesses of inorganic aluminosilicate binders (variability, scale-up cost, incumbency inertia) and shows the geopolymer growth story is led by construction concrete, with wood bonding still niche - the strongest case that silicates may stay marginal.

title: What the EU's new formaldehyde limit means for your press mat application in 2026
date_evidence: ## 30 #### Apr 26 Von: Sebastian Jendrysik  (and in 'Aktuell Posts': 'Faster presses, higher stakes... 30 April, 2026')
key_claim: The pMDI reality: the wood-panel industry's practical formaldehyde-free fallback for E05 compliance is pMDI (polymeric MDI), a highly reactive isocyanate binder that many existing UF resin systems cannot match, but pMDI bonds aggressively to press surfaces, demands specialised release-agent and spray equipment, and carries isocyanate handling hazards.
verbatim_quote: This places many UF-bonded panels at genuine risk of non-compliance unless formulations are significantly modified. This is driving accelerated adoption of pMDI (polymeric methylene diphenyl diisocyanate) and no-added-formaldehyde (NAF) resin systems, both of which can meet the new threshold.
notes: Tier 4: vendor blog by a spray-systems equipment supplier promoting its release-agent products; treat_directionally true and used only as corroboration. This is the single Tier 4 source. Fills role 2 (the pMDI fallback reality) - it is unusually explicit that pMDI, not bio-based glue, is the de facto E05 compliance route and details pMDI's equipment burden and isocyanate hazard. Original-language byline reads German 'Apr 26' / '30 April, 2026'.
